How questions are phrased in surveys **[K]**

How carefully the sample is selected **[K]**

parts.problem_md:
Outline **two** reasons why Gloria might carry out primary market research with her existing customers.

> **[case-study]**
> Gloria is a sole trader. Her business provides house-cleaning services. Gloria uses telephone calls to communicate with her 4 employees. She wants to expand the business by offering a repair service. Gloria plans to carry out some market research. She has been told producing a business plan can help to reduce risk. Gloria would also like to reduce her workload and is considering taking on a business partner.
parts.solution_md:
Primary market research would allow Gloria to determine whether enough of her customers would be interested **[K]** in using her proposed repair service **[Ap]**

It is a convenient group of people to ask **[K]**, as she will already have their contact details from her cleaning business** [Ap]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Outline questions always require you to make use of the case study information to support your points

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Give two valid reasons to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
> - For each reason, refer to the business case study to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Reasons may include:
> 
>   - To find out if there is interest in the new repair service [K] among her existing cleaning customers [Ap]
>   - Easy to access a relevant customer base for feedback [K], as she already has contact details from her current cleaning business [Ap]
>   - To gain direct feedback [K] on what current customers think of the new service idea [Ap]
>   - To reduce risk of failure [K] by asking a familiar and relevant group of customers [Ap]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

Sampling is where market research is conducted **[K]** with a small representative group **[K] **of the market as a whole

> **[exam-tip]**
> Be careful not to confuse sampling, which is a plan to conduct market research, with product samples, which can be a method of market testing

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Sampling is where market research is conducted **[K]** with a small representative group **[K] **of the market as a whole

Market testing is the process of assessing customer reaction **[K]** to a product or service before it is launched **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse market testing, which is assessing consumer reactions to a product, with product testing, which usually focuses on whether a product meets determined standards

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Market testing is the process of assessing customer reaction **[K]** to a product or service before it is launched **[K]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

{align=center} **Protective Hats (PH)**

PH is a large public limited company based in country Z. It has been operating successfully for 50 years. PH produces a range of protective hats for employees working on construction sites, in factories or mines. It has a reputation for producing high-quality products and sells its hats around the world.

PH is currently the market leader in country Z. To remain competitive PH regularly carries out market research to find out if new products are needed. PH needs to ensure its market research data is accurate, so that it can develop the best new protective hats.

PH’s only factory is in country Z. It has 100 production employees. They work on a flow production line and carry out the same tasks every day. PH pays these employees the minimum wage and there have been complaints about working conditions. Some of the employees are considering becoming members of a trade union.

PH’s directors plan to expand the company by opening factories in other countries to produce protective hats. They think there are many benefits for PH of becoming a multinational company. They are aware that there is growing demand for protective hats in many developing countries where construction and manufacturing industries are expected to continue to have strong growth in the next 10 years.

{align=center} Appendix 1

{align=center} Advertisement for PH’s products

{align=center} PH’s protective hats will protect your employees when at work.

{align=center} We supply many of the leading construction, manufacturing and mining companies across the world.

{align=center} High quality is guaranteed.

{align=center} PH’s hats can be ordered online from our website.

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Email to PH’s Managing Director from PH’s Human Resources Director**

To: Managing Director 

From: Human Resources Director 

Date: 1 October 2023 

Re: Training

After reviewing our current training, I think we need to increase the training we provide to new employees. Existing employees would also benefit from additional training as there have been issues with motivation.

I know there are plans to introduce new equipment into the flow production line. When is this likely to happen?

Can we please meet to discuss these issues?

{align=center} **Appendix 3**

{align=center} **PH’s financial data for 2021 and 2022**

|   | **2021** | **2022** |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Revenue | \$100m | \$125m |
| Profit | \$20m | \$20m |
| Gross profit margin | 60% | 65% |
| Profit margin | 20% | 16% |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following three methods PH uses to collect market research data.

- A focus group made up of existing customers
- An online survey with only 5 questions
- Secondary research, including government sources

Which method is most likely to ensure that accurate data is collected? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
A focus group of existing customers allows PH to gain detailed information from people familiar with their products. Customers can discuss their experiences, helping PH understand the reasons behind opinions **[An]**. However, the small sample size may not represent all potential customers of protective equipment **[Ap]**, as it is restricted to existing customers, potentially missing insights about competitors or new market segments **[An]**

An online survey with five questions can quickly reach many customers worldwide. PH already has customer email addresses **[Ap]**, making distribution easy. Results can be automatically analysed using IT, saving time and money **[An]**. However, the small number of questions limits the depth of information gathered. Some customers may rush through it, providing less thoughtful answers than in a focus group **[An]**

Secondary research from government sources is likely reliable and unbiased. It may provide free access to construction industry data **[Ap]**, reducing costs. However, the information could be outdated or too general, not specifically addressing PH's protective hat market, requiring them to carry out further primary research to fill gaps in knowledge **[An]**

The focus group is most likely to ensure accurate data collection **[E]**. While limited in size, it allows PH to gather rich, detailed feedback directly from customers who use their products. PH can probe for specifics about existing hats and requirements for new mining hats **[Ap]**, supporting product development. The interactive discussion reveals nuances that quick online surveys or general government statistics might miss **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Focus group**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Participants already use PH’s protective hats **→** give honest views on good and bad points **→** helps redesign the hat
>     - Group discussion **→** researchers hear the reasons behind each opinion **→** deeper insight
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Sample limited to current customers **→** views may be biased and ignore rivals’ products
>     - Only a few people in the room **→** not enough data for accurate decisions
>     - Hiring a specialist agency and gathering customers **→** can be slow and expensive
> - **Online survey**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Answers fed straight into a computer **→** results analysed quickly and cheaply
>     - Email link reaches many customers worldwide **→** fast response and larger sample
>     - No interviewers or postage **→** costs less than face-to-face or postal surveys
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Only five questions **→** limits the detail of answers
>     - No one on hand to explain questions **→** risk of misunderstanding
>     - Some target customers may lack internet or ignore the email **→** results may not represent the whole market
> - **Secondary research**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Collected by experts **→** usually reliable and unbiased
>     - Often free to access **→** keeps research costs low
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Data may be out of date **→** might not show current trends in mining or construction
>     - Collected for a different purpose **→** may not answer PH’s specific questions about a new hat
>     - Publicly available **→** competitors can use the same figures, so no advantage
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Focus group: provides the most detailed feedback from real users, but its small and possibly biased sample makes results less representative
>   - Online survey: reaches far more people at low cost, yet includes limited questions and no guidance, which can reduce accuracy
>   - Secondary research: quick, cheap and reliable for broad market size, but may be outdated and too general for product design decisions

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Sports Safety Equipment (SSE)

SSE manufactures sports safety equipment in country Z. It is a public limited company which has been successful for over 30 years. The main product SSE manufactures is safety helmets for different sports, such as bicycle riding, cricket and skateboarding. SSE has one large factory making the safety helmets. The factory uses flow production. The production workers each specialise in one task on the production line. SSE’s raw materials are imported.

SSE sells its helmets in several other countries and is planning to expand into many more. It will need to carry out market research before entering new markets in other countries. Each country has different sports that are popular and the style of helmets varies from country to country.

SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries and will need to choose a suitable source of finance. The Human Resources Director has decided to use internal recruitment for the managers of the new factories. There will need to be effective communication between the managers of the new factories and SSE’s head office in country Z.

Most of SSE’s sales in country Z are through sports equipment shops. Customers like to try on the helmets to check they fit correctly. SSE currently sells its helmets in other countries through its website.

SSE is also increasing its product range. The latest new product being developed is a children’s cricket helmet. A break-even chart for this new product is shown in Appendix 3.

{align=center} **Appendix 1**

{align=center} **Extract from SSE’s website**

{align=center} **If you want the best protection when playing sport then buy an SSE safety helmet!**

{align=center} We supply a wide range of safety helmets for you when playing sport. 

Whatever the sport - SSE produces a helmet for you. 

You can order directly from this website by entering your head measurements below. 

Get the perfect fit for you!

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Email from SSE’s Managing Director to SSE’s Finance Director**

To: Finance Director

From: Managing Director

Date: 1 September 2023

Re: Demand for SSE’s products

Demand for SSE’s products in country Z is forecast to increase. Our government has imposed import tariffs on safety helmets. We may be able to increase our prices.

The exchange rate in country Z is expected to fall. However, other countries have introduced import quotas on safety helmets.

We will have to consider all the likely effects of these changes.

{align=center} **Appendix 3**

{align=center} **Projected weekly break-even chart for SSE’s new children’s cricket helmet**

![A graph showing the relationship between output in units (x-axis) and costs and revenue in dollars (y-axis) with lines for total revenue, total costs, and fixed costs.](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/921_nov-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2-2.png)

{align=center} The maximum output and sales for this product is 1000 units per week

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following two methods of market research SSE could use when entering new markets in other countries.

- Primary market research
- Secondary market research

Which method of market research should SSE use? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Primary research would allow SSE to gather up-to-date information about the specific sports and helmet styles **[Ap]** popular in each country. For example, they could survey bicycle riders or cricket players **[Ap]** to understand their exact needs so that SSE could design helmets that meet local preferences. These would stand a good chance of being purchased by customers, which would generate revenue **[An]**. However, primary research can be expensive and time-consuming, especially across multiple countries in which different sports are popular **[Ap]**. This could delay the launch of new products** [An]**

Secondary research would be cheaper and faster for SSE. They could use existing data on the size of the sports equipment market in different countries **[Ap]**. This would help them estimate potential demand for their helmets **[Ap] **and determine whether a market is worth entering **[Ap]**. Secondary sources like newspapers could provide useful economic information about new markets, but this data may be outdated or not specific enough to SSE's helmet business. Primary research may also therefore be needed to fill in the gaps** [An]**

Overall, SSE should use a combination of both methods, but focus more on primary research** [E]**. While more expensive, primary research will provide the most relevant and current data about helmet preferences in each new market **[E]**. This is crucial as SSE is expanding internationally and helmet styles vary between countries **[Ap]**. The specific insights from primary research will help SSE successfully adapt their products for each new market they enter **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Primary market research**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Up-to-date findings about local sports → helmets can be adapted to each country’s popular games (e.g. cricket style) → higher sales potential
>     - Questions focus on sports-helmet buyers’ exact needs → data is specific and reliable → products more likely to meet customer expectations
>     - Research tracks current sporting-trend changes in each market → helps spot opportunities early
>     - Results stay private to SSE → competitors cannot copy the insights
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Interviewer bias or leading questions → answers may be distorted → wrong decisions
>     - Focus groups / interviews cost more → specialist staff need paying → higher research budget
>     - Country-wide questionnaires take time to distribute and analyse → slower launch of helmets
>   - **Secondary market research**
>   
>     - **Advantages**
>     
>       - Often cheaper than doing new surveys → cuts research costs for each target country
>       - Government or trade data shows total market size for cricket helmets → helps forecast demand across new markets
>       - Newspapers and reports reveal the economy’s health → signals whether demand is likely to grow
>       - Information is quick to obtain online → faster preliminary decisions
>     - **Disadvantages**
>     
>       - Statistics on sports like skateboarding may be outdated → misleading for today’s helmet market
>       - Publicly available data → rivals can use the same figures → no competitive edge
>       - Collected for different purposes → may not answer SSE’s specific research questions
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Primary research: best when SSE needs precise, up-to-date insight into customers’ helmet preferences in each new country
>   - Secondary research: best for quickly and cheaply measuring overall market size or economic outlook before deciding whether to enter
>   - Practical approach: start with low-cost secondary data to screen potential markets, then run focused primary research in the most promising countries to fine-tune product design and pricing

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

{align=center} Soapy Sudds Manufacturer (SSM)

SSM is a public limited company that was set up 25 years ago. SSM manufacture soap powder in country Y. The soap powder is used for washing clothes. SSM sells all its soap powder to large retailers in country Y. SSM’s sales have been increasing for many years in country Y but sales in the last year have remained the same. The directors of SSM are considering ways to increase sales.

SSM has a total of 100 employees with 60 in the Operations Department. It uses flow production in the factory and has 10 production lines with 5 workers and 1 supervisor for each line. The Operations Manager is aware that production workers are unhappy and often complain about their jobs being boring. These workers have always been paid by an hourly rate. The Human Resources Manager has recommended changes to ensure fewer workers leave each year to work for other businesses.

The directors of SSM have decided to expand the factory. They will need \$15m to do this. The directors have also considered taking over a competitor. SSM is likely to benefit from economies of scale as it grows.

The Marketing Director thinks SSM should start selling soap powder in markets in other countries. SSM will need to carry out either primary market research or secondary market research to forecast the potential total sales in these new markets. There are many existing manufacturers in these countries. SSM need to consider the problems when entering new markets in other countries such as tariffs or quotas.

{align=center} **Appendix 1**

{align=center} **Manufacturing process to make soap powder**

All the different types of soap powder are manufactured on production lines using flow production. SSM makes use of specialisation.

Each production line has the following stages:

![A flowchart diagram showing soap powder production: Stage 1 - mixing raw materials; Stage 2 - releasing powder onto the conveyor belt; Stage 3 - packaging; Stage 4 - quality checks; Stage 5 - storage.](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/36721_nov-2021-paper-2-case-study.png)

Each of these stages uses machinery controlled by a production worker

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Email from the SSM Finance Director to the Managing Director**

SSM has a cash-flow problem which may get worse. Please see charts below.

![Two bar graphs show the number of days debtors take to pay SSM and the number of days SSM takes to pay suppliers for the years 2019, 2020, and 2021.](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/16229_nov-2021-paper-2-case-study-2.png)

{align=center} **Appendix 3**

{align=center} **Newspaper article from Main News 1 October 2021**

Retailers have reported increased sales for most types of products such as sales of washing machines which have increased by 15%. Economic growth in country Y is predicted to increase.

Many businesses have been recruiting additional employees and there are now shortages of some skilled workers. The government in country Y has recorded an increase in inflation to 8% so far this year, which is a worry.

Consider the advantages of using primary and secondary market research to gather information about the potential sales in the new market. Which is the best method for SSM to use? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2021-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Primary research would allow SSM to collect up-to-date and specific data about customer preferences for soap powder **[Ap]** in the new countries they want to enter. SSM could conduct surveys or focus groups with potential customers to understand their laundry habits **[Ap]** and what features they look for in soap powder. This would give SSM detailed insights that are directly relevant to their products and not available to competitors **[An]**, which could help them to develop detergents that closely meet customer needs and achieve a competitive advantage **[An]**

Secondary research, though, is usually quicker and cheaper to obtain. SSM could access existing market reports or government statistics about the soap powder market in other countries **[Ap]**. This would help SSM understand the overall size of the market and identify any trends. For instance, they could look at data on household spending on laundry products **[Ap]** or population statistics to estimate potential demand. This would help SSM identify which specific markets have the most potential before investing in more costly and time-consuming primary research **[An]**

Overall, secondary research is likely the best method for SSM to use initially **[E]**. As the Marketing Director is considering entering multiple new country markets **[Ap]**, secondary research would allow SSM to efficiently, and at limited cost, gather data on market sizes and trends across different countries. SSM could then follow up with targeted primary research in the most promising markets to gain more detailed customer insights and develop their marketing strategy **[E] **

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Primary market research**
> 
>   - Up-to-date results → reflect customers’ current washing habits
>   - Questionnaire can focus on soap buyers’ likes and dislikes → detailed, reliable feedback for SSM
>   - Findings are private to SSM → rivals cannot copy the data → competitive edge
> - **Secondary market research **
> 
>   - Usually cheaper than carrying out new surveys → cuts research costs
>   - Government statistics show the total soap-powder market size → helps estimate nationwide demand
>   - Data is quick to obtain and can show trends over time → faster, better-informed decisions
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Secondary research is best when SSM needs the overall size of the soap-powder market, because national statistics give wide coverage at low cost
>   - Primary research is best when SSM needs specific details about customers’ washing habits or reactions to its own and competitors’ products, since the questions can be tailored to those exact issues

parts.problem_md:
Explain one method of primary market research and one method of secondary market research Veronique could have used.

> **[case-study]**
> Veronique is bored with her work in a large factory. As a creative person, she would like to leave and start up a flower shop. Veronique has asked about micro-finance and prepared a cash flow forecast. An extract is shown in the below table. Veronique has also carried out some market research and found out that the demand for flowers is likely to be high during festivals. She thinks she has the right characteristics to be a successful entrepreneur.
> 
> | **Extract from the cash flow forecast for Veronique’s flower shop for the first 3 months (\$)** |   |   |   |
> |---|---|---|---|
> |   | Month 1 | Month 2 | Month 3 |
> | Cash in | 500 | 1 200 | 2 000 |
> | Cash out | 1 500 | 1 400 | 1 200 |
> | Net cash flow | (1 000) | (200) | 800 |
> | Opening balance | 0 | (1 000) | (1 200) |
> | Closing balance | (1 000) | (1 200) | (400) |
parts.solution_md:
Veronique could use a questionnaire as a primary market research method **[K]**. This would allow her to gather up-to-date information specific to her flower shop business idea. She could ask potential customers direct questions about their preferences for different types of flowers and arrangements for festivals **[Ap]**. She can then develop displays that fully satisfy their needs **[An]**

For secondary research, Veronique could look at government statistics **[K]**, official figures that would give her data on consumer spending patterns for flowers, especially around festival times **[Ap]**. As government data is usually reliable and covers a broad range of economic indicators, the information could help Veronique take external factors into account in her cash flow forecast for her new business. This could make it more reliable **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For each paragraph:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the business in the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Primary market research:
>   
>     - Questionnaire [k] as provides up-to-date information/specific to her business [an] about trends for festivals [app]
>     - Interviews [k] to obtain in depth details/opinions [an] about different type of flowers [app]
>     - Online survey [k] as more likely to get responses/can reach out to more people [an]
>     - Focus group [k] as provides detailed information about consumer tastes/as allows for follow-up questions [an]
>     - Observation [k] as avoids interviewer bias [an]
>     - Test marketing [k] so the cost of any problem is limited to a smaller number of products [an]
>   - Secondary market research:
>   
>     - Government statistics [k] as being official would provide more accurate data [an] to help her improve her cash flow forecast [app]
>     - Online sources/internet research [k] which is low cost/readily available [an] which can be helpful for a new business [app]
>     - Market research agency reports [k]
>     - Trade associations/data from similar businesses/commercial data [k]
> - Application
> 
>   - To use words from the stem as application, the reference must be appropriate (i.e. make sense) in relation to the point being made
>   - The following words are likely to be appropriate for this question:
>   
>     - Flower (shop)
>     - Festivals
>     - Start-up /new business
>   - Other appropriate examples in context can still be credited

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

{align=center} **The BB Health Spa (BB)**

Bethany owns The BB Health Spa in Main City in country X. Economic growth has been high for the last few years. The government of country X wants this growth to continue so it has reduced income tax. However, it is also worried about inflation becoming a problem so it has increased interest rates.

The BB Health Spa is very busy and Bethany is considering taking on a partner to help manage the business and give her more free time. However, she has been a sole trader for 10 years and wants the business to stay small.

The customers of The BB Health Spa are people of all ages who are interested in their health. Bethany employs two qualified workers to provide the treatments for customers. Bethany herself also provides customers with treatments. In addition, she does all the administration such as ordering inventory, accounts and paying invoices when the spa is closed.

The BB Health Spa still uses the original treatment equipment which was purchased when the business started. Some spas nearby have the latest equipment but these spas charge much higher prices than The BB Health Spa. Bethany records all the financial transactions by filling in accounts books by hand. This takes her a long time. Customers book appointments using the telephone and Bethany later telephones them to remind them when an appointment is due.

{align=center} **Appendix 1**

{align=center} **Advert for treatments at The BB Health Spa**

![Flyer for The BB Health Spa including a massage room, gym equipment, and people doing yoga. Services listed: Sports Therapies, Gym, and Yoga.](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/17946_0450-01-specimen-2020-paper-2-insert-cie-igcse-busines.png)

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Weekly forecasts for two possible additional services**

|   | Steam room | Hair cuts |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Additional customers | 200 | 50 |
| Average price charged per customer | \$5 | \$25 |
| Wages | \$60 | \$400 |
| Cost of sales | \$40 | \$125 |
| Lease of equipment | \$400 | \$175 |

{align=center} **Appendix 3**

**Daily News                                                                                                            September**

{align=center} **New equipment now available in many health spas to make skin look younger**

There have been a number of changes in technology for health spas which allow the treatments to be much more effective in making skin look younger. Many people are keen to try these treatments using the latest equipment to get younger looking skin. This equipment is very expensive for health spas to buy or lease.

The news of these treatments has appeared on social media sites and on mobile phone Apps leading to higher demand. ‘Some customers will pay high prices for such treatments’, said a local health spa owner who is keen to promote his health spa as being one of the first to use the new equipment.

There have also been developments in software which make customer bookings and accounts much easier, quicker and with fewer mistakes. Automatic text (sms) messages are used to remind customers of their appointments – so no need to miss an appointment again.

Look out for these changes in health spas near you!

Explain two reasons why it is important to Bethany to identify changes in customer preferences.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-01-specimen-2020-paper-2-insert-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Bethany needs to identify changes in customer preferences to remain competitive** [K]**.  BB Health Spa uses old equipment, while nearby spas have newer technology, which means treatments are more effective in making skin look younger **[Ap]**. If Bethany doesn't keep up with these changes, customers may switch to competitors offering newer treatments, reducing her sales **[An]**

Secondly, to maintain customer loyalty **[K]**. BB Health Spa's customers are people of all ages who are interested in their health **[Ap]** and are keen to try treatments using the latest equipment to get younger looking skin. If Bethany doesn't identify and respond to this changing preference, her loyal customers may become dissatisfied and stop visiting the spa. This could lead to a loss of regular business and damage BB Health Spa's reputation **[An]**

> - In each paragraph:
> 
>   - State one valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain how it works using a cause–effect chain → up to 2 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant reasons might include:
> • to meet customer needs
> • to remain competitive
> • keep a good reputation
> • keep customer loyalty/maintain demand

parts.problem_md: Explain two methods of primary market research a business could use to find out the demand for a new product or service. Which would be the best method to use? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Questionnaires collect customers’ opinions and preferences** [K]**. They’re quick to distribute to many people and can target the right audience **[An]**, but responses may lack detail **[An]**

Interviews gather more in-depth information from customers **[K].** Follow-up questions help explore views further [An], though they take longer and are harder to analyse **[An]**

Interviews are the better method **[E]**, as detailed responses help understand what customers want in a new product** [E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - (Postal) questionnaire/survey [k] – apply to either method:
> 
>   - Customer opinions/preferences/suggestions can be gathered [an]
>   - Large amounts of information can be collected [an]
>   - Detailed information can be gathered [an]
>   - Allows many people to be asked (the same questions) [an]
>   - Questions may be poorly worded/difficult to phrase questions properly/people interpret questions in a different way [an]
>   - People may not tell the truth/say what they think sounds good [an]
>   - Customers may not complete/return the questionnaires [an]
>   - May have to pay someone with the right skills to design the questionnaire properly [an] which increases the cost [an]
> - **Online survey [k] **– additional specific points
> 
>   - Data can be quickly presented/analysed using IT tools [an]
>   - Fast/quicker response time (than other forms of survey) [an]
>   - Cheaper** than **interviews/postal questionnaire/focus group etc. [an]
>   - No representative needed to carry it out [an]
> - (Postal) questionnaire/survey [k] – additional specific points
> 
>   - Carrying out questionnaire takes time/money [an]
>   - Analysing results takes time [an]
> - Some points could be written as either advantages or disadvantages of different methods but only award once
> - Some points can be awarded as [k] or [an] but only award once

parts.problem_md: Do you think it is always better for a start-up business to use primary market research, rather than secondary market research, when making decisions? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Primary market generates relevant and up-to-date data **[K]**, helping find out exactly what a start-up business wants to know. However, it's expensive and time-consuming to carry out and analyse surveys, interviews or focus groups. A new business might struggle to afford it without taking funds from other areas of the business that require investment at the start** [An]**

Secondary research is usually cheaper, or free** [K]**,  which can help reduce costs, an important consideration for start-ups with limited finances. However, secondary data may be outdated or irrelevant, potentially leading to a new business owner making inappropriate decisions, which may impact its early success **[An]**

The best approach depends on the specific needs and resources of the start-up **[E]**. A combination of both methods might be ideal. For example, a start-up could use cheap secondary research for general market trends, then conduct small-scale primary research to verify key points, balancing cost and relevance **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Primary market research:
>   
>     - Relevant / up to date data gathered [k] so should help you find out what you want to know [an]
>     - High cost / time to collect information [k] which a new business might not be able to afford [an]
>     - Only available to own business [k]
>     - May find it difficult to find people that represent target market /population [k]
>   - Secondary market research:
>   
>     - May not be relevant / outdated [k] which can lead to wrong decisions [an]
>     - Readily available [k]
>     - Cheap [k]
>     - Can collect wide range of information [k]
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Primary research collects business specific data [k] helping to find out what you want to know [an]. Secondary research is cheaper than primary to collect [k] which could help reduce costs [an]. As this is a start-up business finance may be limited therefore secondary research may be better for them. [eval]. However the information must be from a reliable source. [eval]
> - Some points could be awarded for different options, but do not award the same point twice
> - For evaluation to be awarded justification will usually follow on from relevant analysis of points
> - Do not accept mirror arguments such as primary research is up to date and secondary research maybe outdated

{align=center} **Titantic Toys (TT)**

TT is a large manufacturer of toys based in country Y. It is a public limited company and has been trading for 20 years. TT’s products are designed for children up to the age of 5.

parts.problem_md:
Calculate the percentage of people who buy beauty products online. Show your working.

> **[case-study]**
> GBU is a public limited company. It makes a range of beauty products, including shampoo and soaps for the mass market.
> 
> Last year, GBU’s revenue fell. The Marketing Director has been looking at some results from its primary market research. It was based on a sample of 2000 people, see Table 4.1. She believes maintaining customer loyalty is more important than attracting new customers.
> 
> Table 4.1: Market research
> 
> | Question 1: Where do you buy beauty products? |   |   |
> |---|---|---|
> | Shop | Online | Mail order |
> | 1,100 | 700 | 200 |
> 
> | Question 2: Do you buy GBU beauty products? |   |
> |---|---|
> | Yes | No |
> | 1,700 | 300 |
parts.solution_md:
**35%** **[2]**

**Calculation steps**

Add shop, online and mail order customers to calculate the total number of customers

$=1,100+700+200\,\,=2,000\mathrm{customers}$

Divide the number of online customers by the total number of customers

$=700\div2,000\,\,=0.35$    **[1]**

Multiple the outcome by 100 to calculate the percentage

$= 0.35 \\times 100 = 35 \%$    **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Application, 2
> 
>   - Show your workings and express your final answers clearly to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Method, e.g. (700/2000) $\times$ 100 (1)
> - Final answer 35% (1)
> - If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks
